name: SECURITY GUARD ROOM
text: This monitoring station feels lived-in, a
cramped pocket of surveillance tucked away
from the main corridors. The concrete walls
and functional furniture speak to its

msg: Among the notices: a STAMPED TRAVEL
PERMIT with your name pencilled in.

name: METAL LOCKER UNIT
text: A standard-issue double locker, its grey paint
chipped and worn from regular use. One side
stands open, revealing a coat and hat.

name: CONTROL DESK WITH MONITORS
text: A sturdy control console sits beneath a bank
of CRT monitors, its surface crowded with a
keyboard, switches, and a solitary coffee mug.
The screens display grainy feeds of empty

name: OPEN LOCKER COMPARTMENT
text: Inside the open locker hangs a heavy brown
coat, looking well-worn and warm. A dark green
helmet rests on the shelf above.

name: NARROW COT BED
text: A simple metal-framed cot is tucked against
the wall, covered with a rumpled brown blanket
and a flat white pillow. It looks like it sees
more use for quick naps than full nights of

name: FLOOR SEAM DETAILS
text: Thick metal plating covers the floor, with
prominent seams forming a large cross pattern
in the center of the room. The surface is
scuffed and shows the grey color underneath

name: ROW OF SECURITY MONITORS
text: Four small CRT monitors are bracketed
together, forming the top row of the
surveillance setup. They show various static
views of concrete tunnels and utilitarian

name: CORK BULLETIN BOARD
text: A framed corkboard hangs on the wall,
cluttered with pinned papers, a map, and a few
faded photographs. It serves as a makeshift
command center and personal space for the

name: RUMPLED BED BLANKET
text: The brown blanket on the cot is carelessly
tossed, suggesting someone left in a hurry or
just woke up. It looks thick enough to ward
off the chill of the concrete room.

name: TALL CORKBOARD
text: A second, taller corkboard is mounted on the
side wall, holding more maps and notices. It
helps organize the paperwork needed to manage
this sector.

name: PINNED NOTES AND MAP
text: Close-up on the bulletin board reveals a hand-
drawn map of the local tunnel network,
alongside various typed memos and a couple of
ID photos.

name: OPEN LOCKER DOOR
text: The metal door of the locker is swung open,
its inner surface detailed with small
ventilation slits. The grey paint is scratched
near the handle.

name: CLOSED LOCKER DOOR
text: The left side of the locker unit remains
firmly shut, keeping its contents hidden. The
metal surface is plain, save for the
horizontal vents near the bottom.

name: LOWER SECURITY MONITORS
text: The bottom row of the monitor bank shows more
feeds of dim, concrete corridors. The screens
cast a cool, pale glow over the control desk.
